newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - December 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - December 23.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A judicial magistrate remanded Asif Ali Zardari to the custody of the Crimes Branch for interrogation till December 26.
- A total of 9,450 candidates filed their nomination papers for the 700 national and provincial assembly seats throughout the country, Election Commission said.
- The caretaker government of the southern Sindh province has lifted a three-year-old ban on issuance of arms licences.

- The United Arab Emirates has expressed regrets that it could not accede to Pakistan's request for $350 million saying that the matter could be considered only when a new government was in place after the February 3 elections.
- Shahid Javed Burki, adviser on finance to the caretaker prime minister, asked Pakistanis living in the United Arab Emirates to bid for state units being privatised.
- The state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan asked bidders to match the lowest bid by Monday for the supply of 50,000 tonnes of refined sugar for delivery upto January 11.
- The state-run Pakistan International Airlines has deferred an increase of 15 percent in fares to Jeddah and Madinah until further notice.

- A few days before talks with the International Monetary Fund for seeking a $600 million stand-by loan, the caretaker government borrowed $120 million from a Dubai-based gold trade tycoon to raise its foreign exchange reserves.

- Violating his own commitment to austerity, the cricketer-turned politician Imran Khan has hired a helicopetr for 30 million rupees for his election campaign and paid four million rupees to build a most modernised truck with a mobile stage to address election rallies.
- Pakistan, Iran and Turkey are meeting in Ankara on January 4 and 5 to discuss ways for promoting peace and national reconciliation in war-ravaged Afghanistan.
